title: Human Fibroblast Reprogramming to Naïve Induced Pluripotent Stem Cells in Microfluidics
protocol: Design the photomask using CAD or Illustrator software.
Print the photomask on a transparency film in high-resolution (>2400 dpi).
Wash the silicon wafer with 2-Propanol.
Wash the silicon wafer with distilled water.
Dry the wafer on a hot plate at 120°C for 30 minutes.
Place the wafer on the chuck of the spin coater and power the vacuum pump.
Dispense 1 ml of photoresist for each inch of wafer diameter.
Spin the wafer at 500 r.p.m. for 10 s with acceleration of 100 r.p.m/s.
Spin the wafer at 500 r.p.m. for 30 s with acceleration of 1500 r.p.m/s.
Bake the coated wafer on a hot plate at 65°C for 5 minutes.
Bake the coated wafer on a hot plate at 95°C for 30 minutes.
Expose the photoresist through a photomask to UV light at exposure energy of 310 mJ/cm².
Bake the coated wafer on a hot plate at 65°C for 5 minutes.
Bake the coated wafer on a hot plate at 95°C for 10 minutes.
Place the wafer in a glass dish and put it on a shaker.
Pour propylene glycol monomethyl ether acetate into the glass and shake for 15 minutes.
Wash the wafer with 2-Propanol.
Dry the wafer with compressed air.
Bake the coated wafer on a hot plate at 80°C for 1 hour.
Place the patterned wafer in a Petri dish and then in a desiccator.
Add a small beaker with few drops of hexamethyldisilazane \(HMDS\) to the desiccator.
Connect the desiccator to the vacuum line to reduce pressure inside the desiccator.
Keep the wafer under vacuum for 30 minutes.
Pour Sylgard 184 PDMS in a plastic cup in a 10:1 base:curing-agent ratio.
Mix the PDMS thoroughly for at least 3 minutes.
Place the uncured PDMS in a desiccator and connect it to the vacuum line.
Keep the PDMS under vacuum to remove bubbles.
Vent the desiccator after 15 minutes.
Place the wafer with PDMS into the vacuum desiccator for 10 minutes.
Check for complete removal of bubbles in the PDMS.
Place the Petri dish containing both the wafer and PDMS in an oven.
Cure it at 70°C for 1.5 hours.
Separate the cured PDMS block from the wafer.
Cut the PDMS block into pieces according to the pattern of the wafer.
Use disposable 1-mm biopsy punches to produce inlet and outlet holes for each culture chamber.
Prepare the reservoirs as PDMS pieces of 5 x 0.5 cm.
Punch the PDMS pieces with a 3-mm biopsy punch.
Clean thoroughly a microscopy glass slide with MICRO-90 cleaning solution \(2% v/v in distilled water).
Rinse the glass slide with distilled water.
Place the PDMS replica, with the patterned surface facing up, and a glass slide in an air plasma cleaner.
Surface activate at 0.3 mbar of filtered air and 30 W for 2 minutes.
Place in conformal contact the activated surfaces of both PDMS and glass.
Place the device with the PDMS surface up into an air plasma cleaner at 0.3 mbar of filtered air and 30 W for 2 minutes.
Seal the PDMS reservoir by placing it in conformal contact with the flat side of the PDMS.
Place the device in an oven at 80°C for 1 hour to complete the bonding process.
Cool the bonded microfluidic device to room temperature.
Pipette 12 µL of 2-propanol inside each culture chamber to clean from production by-products.
Rinse the chambers with 30 µL of distilled water before evaporating the 2-propanol.
Dry the chambers by aspirating the water with a 200 µL pipette.
Package the microfluidic device inside an autoclave bag.
Autoclave at 121°C for 15 minutes, and let it dry at the end.
Resuspend each mmRNA (POU5F1, SOX2, MYC, KLF4, NANOG) with or without nGFP following the manufacturer's datasheet.
Mix POU5F1 at 520 μl, KLF4 at 183 μl, SOX2 at 155 μl, cMYC at 200 μl, and NANOG at 136 μl together in the specified molar ratios.
Aliquot mixed mmRNAs into small amounts (5 to 10 μl) in sterile microtubes.
Avoid freezing-and-thawing more than twice for stored aliquots of mixed mmRNAs.
Supplement DMEM with 10% FBS and optionally add antibiotics, though reprogramming can be performed without them.
Add B18R at a final concentration of 0.2 μg/ml to the complete Primed Reprogramming Medium when reprogramming starts.
Do not store the medium containing B18R for more than 72 hours.
Add RI at 5 μM and CH at 1 μM only when reprogramming begins, ensuring they are not stored beyond 72 hours.
Add B18R at a final concentration of 0.2 μg/ml to RSeT medium only upon initiation of reprogramming.
Do not store the RSeT medium with added B18R for more than 72 hours.
Seed human fibroblasts in microfluidics (µF) chip on Day -1.
Place the µF chip inside a 100 mm cell culture dish.
Add 3 ml PBS-/- to the 100mm cell culture dish containing the µF chip.
Prepare a 25 μg/ml fibronectin solution in PBS-/-.
Inject 12 µl of fibronectin solution into each channel.
Incubate for 30 min at room temperature.
Calculate the number of fibroblasts needed for reprogramming, aiming for 25 cells/mm² with a total surface of one channel being ~27 mm² (thus requiring 675 cells per channel).
Detach fibroblasts by washing twice with PBS-/-.
Add trypsin and incubate at 37°C for 3-4 minutes.
Add at least three volumes of Fibroblast Medium to the cell suspension.
Transfer the cell suspension into a sterile 15 ml tube.
Count fibroblasts with chamber and transfer the calculated number to a sterile tube.
Spin the cell suspension at 300 rcf for 4 minutes in a benchtop microcentrifuge.
Resuspend the cell pellet in fresh Fibroblast Medium.
Inject 12 µl of cell suspension per channel.
Remove excess liquid from reservoirs, leaving enough medium to form a meniscus.
Culture overnight in a low oxygen incubator at 37°C with CO2 at 5% and O2 at 5%.
Calculate the total volume of PRM needed for the first 3 days of reprogramming experiment.
Add RI (5 µM), CH (1 µM), and B18R (0.2 µg/ml) to the complete PRM medium.
Do not store the prepared PRM medium for more than 3 days.
Leave the complete PRM medium at room temperature for at least 30 minutes before use.
Add 12 µl of PRM medium to each channel.
Remove excess exhausted medium from reservoirs.
Transfer µF chips back into the incubator for at least 1 hour before transfection.
Thaw mmRNA aliquots on ice.
Mix A: Mix 0.27 μl TB with 0.09 μl mmRNAs in RNase-free sterile tubes.
Mix B: Mix 0.333 μl TB with 0.027 μl TR in RNase-free sterile tubes.
Transfer Mix B to Mix A and mix gently 4-5 times.
Incubate the transfection mix for 20 min at RT.
Gently transfer 0.7 μl of Mix A+B to a tube containing 11.3 μl of complete PRM.
Mix gently 4-5 times.
Dispense 12 μl of the mix to each channel.
Incubate in Low oxygen incubator (37°C, CO2 5%, O2 5%) for 8 hours.
Warm complete PRM at 37°C and add 12 μl to each channel.
Remove excess of exhausted medium from reservoirs.
Incubate in Low oxygen incubator (37°C, CO2 5%, O2 5%) overnight.
Check for nuclear EGFP after first transfection. Expect >50% nEGFP+ cells.
Proceed with transfection as described in point 3.
Gradually increase the amount of mmRNA transfected starting from day 2 if fibroblasts appear healthy and proliferative.
Do not increase the mmRNA amount if cell population is steady or stressed.
Estimate mmRNA transfection efficiency by looking at nuclear EGFP signal.
Increase mmRNA amount by multiplying volumes indicated in point 3 by 1.25X, 1.5X, or 1.75x as needed.
Typically increase the mmRNA amount every second day, reaching a 1.75x amount by day 5-6.
Add fresh complete PRM at 6 p.m.
Monitor fibroblasts for Mesenchymal to Epithelial Transition (MET) over the first 6 days.
Restart the protocol if MET is not observed.
If MET is observed, switch cells to RSeT medium from Day 6 onwards.
Calculate the amount of complete RSeT medium needed as done for PRM in point 2a.
Add B18R at a concentration of 0.2 µg/ml to RSeT and store complete RSeT at 4°C for maximum 72 hours.
Prepare transfection using RSeT instead of PRM from day 6 onwards, typically using the 1.75x dose of mmRNA until the end of the reprogramming protocol (day 12).
Wash twice with PBS-/- each channel containing naïve iPSC colonies.
Incubate cells with 12 µl Accutase (or TrypLE) for 3-7 min at room temperature.
Add 12 µl of RSeT to each channel when all cells are fully detached.
Collect cells from reservoir into a 1.5 ml microtube.
Add 1 ml RSeT with 10 µM RI to the 1.5 ml microtube and plate on inactivated MEF in a well of a 24-well plate.
Add 0.6 ml of fresh RSeT medium every day and passage colonies every 3-5 days according to colony size and proliferation level.
Use a split ratio between 1:1 and 1:4 based on the number of colonies, their size, and proliferation rate.
Passage naïve iPSC lines every 5-6 days at a split ratio of 1:1 for the first two passages when starting from 3 colonies.
Obtain stable niPSC lines after 2 passages at a split ratio of 1:2 to 1:3 every 3 days when starting with more than 50 colonies.
Routinely passage stable niPSC lines every 3-4 days at a split ratio of 1:3 to 1:4, changing the medium daily under low oxygen conditions on feeder cells.
Check naïve pluripotent identity during expansion by quantitative real-time RT PCR and immunostaining as described in Figures 2 and S2 of Giulitti et al., 2018.
